extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in automated theorem proving, formal methods, and ML-for-code/LLM-for-theorem-proving
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating systems that combine large language model whole-proof synthesis with tactic-level generation and refinement to produce formal proofs (implemented here for Isabelle). Focus is on model architectures, dataset preparation, integration with automated tools, and empirical evaluation on benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid approach combining tactic-based and whole-proof generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines tactic-based generation and whole-proof synthesis to harness the benefits of both approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate whole-proof candidates to explore proof possibilities and use tactic-based generation to produce verifiable, stepwise proofs; the combination should improve success over either approach alone (the paper attributes SOTA performance to this combination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-proof candidate generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate whole proof candidates for evaluation directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an LLM to synthesize complete proof texts/candidates which can be evaluated and from which sketches can be extracted; whole-proof generation serves as a source of diverse proof ideas and seeds for refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof sketch extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract proof sketches from whole-proof candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive higher-level sketches or outlines from synthesized full proofs to serve as inputs for a tactic-based generator that completes details; extraction should preserve the essential structure while enabling stepwise tactic refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic-based generation with integration of automated tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a tactic-based generation model that integrates automated tools to complete the sketches via stepwise refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine LLM-driven tactic selection/production with automated theorem-proving tools (e.g., tactics, automation inside the prover) to iteratively build and verify proofs; emphasize stepwise, verifiable refinements rather than only free-form text proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-tune LLMs on optimized Isabelle datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement the system for the Isabelle theorem prover and fine-tune LLMs on optimized Isabelle datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and optimize domain-specific datasets for the target prover (Isabelle here) and fine-tune models on that data to improve proof synthesis performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark evaluation using miniF2F success rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate on benchmark datasets (miniF2F) and measure success rate (the paper reports a 59.4% success rate on miniF2F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard benchmarks and clear success metrics (e.g., solved_theorem_percentage) and compare to prior SOTA (the paper reports prior SOTA 56.1%) to quantify improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ablation studies to attribute performance gains
rubrics_metrics.description: Run ablation studies to show which components are responsible for gains (the paper's ablations indicate SOTA is attributable to combining whole-proof and tactic-based generation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically remove or modify components (e.g., whole-proof path, tactic-based path, dataset variants) and report impact to support causal claims about design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of dataset quality, training parameters, and sampling diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset quality, training parameters, and sampling diversity affect final results during automated theorem proving with LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and report how dataset curation/quality, hyperparameters/optimization choices, and generation/sampling diversity influence performance; tune these aspects as part of system development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source release for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All code, datasets, and LLMs are open source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release artifacts (code, datasets, trained models) to enable reproducibility and community use; this supports validation and further research.
